Name: queue alerts
Description: Ines: Sixteen minutes blind. Okay, that's finding number one. Let's make it concrete: alerting on queue depth for the payment workers, warning at 1,000 jobs, page at 5,000. Kofi, yours? Kofi: Yeah, I'll take it. Honestly the whole worker fleet should have that alert, not just payments, same thresholds everywhere. I'll do it in one pass.

Name: retry fix with dead-letter queue
Description: Kofi: Right, root cause. The retry logic in the payment worker. When the card processor returned 503s, our workers retried immediately, no backoff, no jitter. Every failure multiplied the load. Classic retry storm, we DDoSed ourselves. Marta: I read that code yesterday. The retry loop is in payment_worker.py, the _process_with_retry function. It retries five times back to back, and, this is the good part, on the fifth failure it re-enqueues the job at the front of the queue. Ines: The front? That's incredible. Okay, that's the second action and it's the big one: fix the retry logic. Exponential backoff with jitter, cap the retries, and failed jobs go to a dead-letter queue at the back, not the front of the main one. Marta, you've clearly already got context, can you own it? Marta: Yep. I'll add tests that simulate processor 503s too, because clearly nothing covered this.

Name: connection pool split
Description: Kofi: While we're in there, the DB connection pool made everything worse. Once workers piled up, they exhausted the pool, which is still at the default of 20 connections, and that's when the API started failing too. That's the coupling. Ines: So two things there? Bump the pool, and stop the workers from sharing the API's pool? Kofi: Honestly, bumping it to 100 gets us through the next incident, and splitting worker and API pools is the real fix. I'd do both in one change, it's the same config file. I'll take that one.

Name: runbook refresh with Priya
Description: Ines: Fine, one task, both parts, Kofi. Now, the human side. Priya was on call. She did fine, but she told me the runbook for payment incidents still references the old Kibana, which we turned off in March. She spent ten minutes on dead links. Marta: Oh no. Ines: Yeah. So: update the payment incident runbook. New logging links, the queue drain procedure Kofi improvised on Tuesday, actually written down, and while we're at it, verify the escalation phone numbers are current, apparently one of them still goes to someone who left last year. Kofi: Priya said she'd be up for doing that herself, she's got the freshest scars. Let's assign it to her, I'll confirm with her after this.

Name: status page automation
Description: Ines: Good. Next: status page. We didn't update it until minute 30, and customers noticed. Support got fifty tickets in that window, most of them just asking if we knew. Marta: The status page update is manual, that's why. Someone has to remember, log in, click through three screens. We should automate it: when the checkout error rate alert fires, the status page flips to investigating automatically, with a template message. Ines: Take that one too? It's small, the status provider has an API. Marta: Sure, I'll wire it to the checkout alert first, we can extend it to other alerts later.

Name: failover game day plan
Description: Kofi: Can I raise one more? This incident would've been a non-event if failover worked. We have a secondary payment processor configured, in theory. It's never been exercised. Nobody wanted to be the person who tests it in production. Ines: So let's be those people, deliberately. A game day: controlled chaos test of the payment processor failover in staging first, then production during a low-traffic window, with a rollback plan. That's bigger, let's say Kofi leads it and drafts the plan, and we review the plan in two weeks before anything gets executed. Draft first, no execution until the review. Kofi: Deal. I'll write it up.

Name: Redis upgrade
Description: Ines: Ha, add it to the backlog for 2030. Okay, last thing. Redis. Kofi, you mentioned in the channel that we're on an EOL version? Kofi: Yeah, 6.0, security fixes ended in June. Not related to the outage, but since we're listing infra debt: we should upgrade to 7.2. It's a minor migration, there's a config rename and the persistence defaults changed, so it needs a proper change window, not a casual Friday deploy. Ines: Agreed, that's a real one, Kofi owns it, schedule it with the infra calendar.
